name: Run Cloud

modes.label: Linux microVM, minimal CPU floor + auto-burst (deprecated)
modes.note: Reserve a small CPU floor (min 0.125 vCPU) and let the VM auto-burst: billed CPU per second = max(reserved, consumed) at the same rate (burst is a separate 'CPU (burst)' invoice line, measured from the cgroup). Encoded as active basis with floor 0 (the 0.125 vCPU floor is negligible). vCPU rate DERIVED from the docs worked example (525 burst vCPU-s ~ $0.0034 => ~$0.0233/vCPU-h; rounding band $0.0230-0.0237). Memory billed on reservation (hard ceiling) but the RAM rate is NOT published. Burst ceiling above the reservation undocumented. Not available to new organizations. [basis verified 2026-09-28] Docs: "Your reserved vCPU is the billing floor and is always charged while the sandbox runs." / "CPU actually consumed above the floor bills as a separate CPU (burst) invoice line" / "Memory bills on the reservation" (docs.run.cloud/sandboxes/index.md). Per-second billed CPU = max(reserved, consumed): kept "active" (engine "max" means pay the full requested size); floor 0 because the 0.125 vCPU default floor is ~3% of 4 vCPU. Idle auto-pause via SDK idlePauseSeconds ("set it to 0 to disable automatic pause", computesdk run-cloud README); paused billing ambiguous.

modes.label: Linux microVM, full CPU reserved (deprecated)
modes.note: Same rate; reserving the full vCPU count makes the reservation the billing floor for the whole run regardless of utilisation. Only useful to guarantee capacity (reserved CPU counts against the 100-vCPU org cap; burst does not). Never cheaper than floor-burst. [basis verified 2026-09-28] Docs: "You are billed per second of runtime against the resources you reserved." (docs.run.cloud/sandboxes/index.md).

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Only plan. First $15 of usage free every month once a payment method is added (applies to sandbox burst too); $5 of usage allowed with no card. Org caps: 100 sandboxes (incl. paused/stopped, not destroyed), 100 reserved vCPU, 400 GiB reserved RAM, 100 tunnels; raisable by operators. Unpaid-usage ceiling $500 with card (prepaid credit raises it; owner can set a lower spend limit); hitting it stops active sandboxes. Sandboxes are closed to new organizations.

extras.item: iOS simulator / Android emulator session (current product)

perf_source: StarSling hpc-sandbox-benchmarks, run 36498291449 (2026-09-29), Node.js V8 Web Tooling p50 at a 4 vCPU / 8 GB target
caveats: DEPRECATED: Linux microVM sandboxes are no longer available to new organizations (docs banner, 2026-09-28); removal date unpublished. Both modes and the plan are flagged legacy.
vCPU rate $0.0233/h is derived from a rounded docs example (75 vCPU-s ~ $0.0005 floor, 525 vCPU-s ~ $0.0034 burst); no rate card is published. Band ~$0.0230-0.0237.
Memory is billed on reservation but its rate is unpublished (ram_gib_h null): any estimate is CPU-only and understates the bill.

Whether paused/stopped sandboxes bill anything is ambiguous: docs say billing is 'per second of runtime' but also 'billing stops when the sandbox is destroyed', and paused/stopped sandboxes keep consuming org capacity slots.
Snapshot storage 'is not metered today' ($0), with a hint it may change. Disk quota is configurable but disk price unpublished.
Egress, ingress, IPv4 prices unpublished; inbound only via expiring tunnel hostnames (default TTL 1 h).
Free: $5 without a card; $15/month with a card (encoded as one-time 5 + monthly 15; whether they stack is unclear).
Current run.cloud product is mobile simulators at $0.02/active minute (listed in extras, not a Linux sandbox mode).
Only benchmark: burst TTI median 15.8 s at 100 concurrency; every DAX run failed.

fleet.tiers: Legacy-only organization limits were 100 retained sandboxes, 100 reserved vCPU and 400 GiB RAM; not offered to new organizations.
fleet.notes: Official limits page now explicitly deprecates Linux microVM sandboxes and closes them to new organizations. New-customer fleet is unavailable (0), regardless of historical quotas. iOS/Android/Xcode products unaffected but are not this card. Legacy quota reviews require org ID, requested numbers, workload/duration, deadline and billing/capacity review; no SLA.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Pausing writes the sandbox's RAM to disk, and archiving uploads it, so both hold whatever the sandbox held.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: idle auto-pause (`idlePauseSeconds` / `--idle-pause <seconds>`: 'Pause after inactivity; use `0` to keep the sandbox running', https://docs.run.cloud/cli/latest.md). Pause keeps disk AND memory (SDK: 'Halt the sandbox, keeping disk and memory; compute billing stops.', https://docs.run.cloud/sdk/latest.md); `sandbox shell` auto-resumes a paused sandbox, exec needs an explicit resume. Paused sandboxes may be 'archived' (RAM uploaded). What happens at the `--timeout` lifetime (default 300 s) is not documented (likely destroy, not pause). Deprecated product, closed to new orgs.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A snapshot captures a sandbox's filesystem so you can restore it later.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Filesystem only (no memory; secrets held in memory are not included). Restore 'produces a **new** sandbox with its own id. The snapshot is not consumed, so one snapshot can fan out into as many sandboxes as you need' (fork/template). Snapshot storage 'not metered today'. Manual pause/resume separately preserves memory for the same sandbox, but is not forkable.

harness_api.quote: Persistent sandboxes boot `runcloud/agent-base`, which ships Node.js, Python, and SSH but no coding-agent CLIs. Install the one you want after connecting
harness_api.note: Full SDK/CLI reference (sdk/latest.md, cli/latest.md) exposes only create/exec/readFile/writeFile/tunnels/snapshot/pause for sandboxes; no agent-session API. 'Agent skills' are instructions for YOUR local coding agent to drive run.cloud, not a harness API. Claude Code must be installed manually via SSH.

ingress_rules.quote:
Tunnel hostnames are random bearer capabilities. Do not write them to public logs.
They expire automatically and are removed when the tunnel or sandbox is deleted.
ingress_rules.note: Nothing is exposed by default; you choose the port. Two models: short-lived random-hostname tunnels (`openTunnel(id, port, { ttlSeconds })`, default TTL 1 h, max 8 per sandbox) and a stable public `<name>-box.run.cloud` hostname (`sandbox expose --port`, one per sandbox, custom domains) that appears to have no auth. SSH is carried 'over an authenticated connection' without opening port 22. No IP allowlists/security groups documented. Desktop noVNC URLs are signed temporary bearer URLs with a view-only mode.

guest_firewall.note: Firecracker microVM 'with its own kernel, not a container' (sandboxes/index.md) and the card has root; whether the guest kernel ships nftables/iptables modules is not documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Anything running in the sandbox can read the sandbox's secrets.
secret_proxy.note: Secret groups are delivered as plain env vars in every exec and as files under the home directory (held in memory, not on disk, so not captured in snapshots/forks). No injecting proxy.

volume_attach.note: Only a per-sandbox writable disk quota (`--disk <gb>` 'Set root disk capacity in GiB'); the complete CLI and SDK references list no volume/mount noun.

volume_shared.quote: Sandboxes are the single compute noun.
volume_shared.note: No shared volume or bucket mount in the CLI/SDK references; sharing state is done via snapshots (fan-out copies, not a shared live FS).

usage_api.quote: usage({ orgId? }) returns Promise<UsageReport>. UsageReport.items contains cumulative usage entries with org_id, meter, and seconds.
usage_api.note: granularity: per-organization; cost: no; SDK-based API only; no REST endpoint documented. Linux microVM sandboxes deprecated and closed to new orgs; mobile simulators (iOS/Android) are the current product. Usage reports metrics (seconds/meter), not cost; separate account balance API exists but usage endpoint provides quantities only.
